title: Catalogue
intro: What you sell and what you record about the people who buy it. Tel-Agent ships with none of this — the assistant only ever speaks from what you put here.
svc_consultation_says: The full first appointment. We look at the whole job before quoting.
svc_first_says: Short and free of charge for new customers.
svc_onsite_says: We come to you, usually within the same week.
svc_phone_says: Booked like any other slot, held by phone.
svc_emergency_says: Arranged with a person, never booked automatically.
services_note: A service switched off still shows in your own calendar — it just stops being offered on the phone. The assistant then says it exists but has to be arranged with a person.
fields_note: The columns your contact list has. Two of them are fixed because a phone system cannot work without them; everything else is yours to define, and each field says separately whether the assistant may read it out.
field_name_note: Used in the greeting when the number is known.
field_number_note: How a caller is recognised at all.
field_appointments_note: Past and upcoming, read from the calendar.
field_consent_note: Decides whether campaigns may call this contact.
field_customer_no_note: Your own reference from the accounting system.
field_balance_note: Synced nightly from the accounting system.
field_internal_note: What colleagues write about a customer.
fields_warning: A field the assistant may read can be spoken to whoever is on the line. It has no way to know that the person calling from a number is the person the record belongs to — so keep anything you would not say to a stranger switched off.
preview_heading: What the assistant can say now
preview_note: Generated from the catalogue, not written by hand. Change a price here and the sentence changes on the next call.
say_price_q: How much is a first appointment?
say_price_a: The first consultation is thirty minutes and free of charge. A full consultation is sixty minutes at a hundred and twenty euro.
say_onsite_a: Yes — an on-site visit takes about ninety minutes and is charged at the hourly rate. Usually within the same week.
say_urgent_q: I need someone today, it is urgent.
say_urgent_a: An emergency call-out has to be arranged with a colleague. I will have someone ring you straight back.
say_urgent_from: From Emergency call-out — booking is switched off
say_balance_q: What do I still owe you?
say_balance_a: I cannot see that here. A colleague will call you back with the figure.
say_balance_from: Outstanding balance is hidden from the assistant
gap_cancellation: No service has a cancellation window, so the assistant cannot say how late a booking can be moved.
gap_emergency_price: Emergency call-out has no price at all — callers asking are told a person will ring back.
gap_consent: Consent date is hidden, which is why campaigns skip 39 contacts.
used_calendar: Booking uses the lengths set here
empty_services_body: Until something is here the assistant can take messages but cannot book anything, and any question about what you offer or what it costs gets “I don’t know”.
empty_fields_body: Those two exist because a phone system cannot recognise a caller without them. Every other column is one you define — a customer number, a consent date, whatever your work needs.
empty_preview_body: These sentences are generated from the catalogue, so an empty catalogue produces none. Asked what you offer or what it costs, the assistant says it cannot say and offers to have somebody ring back — that is all it can honestly do.
dialog_note: One line the assistant can quote, book and price.
form_price_note: Leave empty and the assistant says the price depends on the job.
form_says_placeholder: We come to you, usually within the same week.
bookable_on: Offered on the phone and booked into a free slot without asking anyone.
bookable_off: Mentioned on the phone, but the caller is told a person will arrange it.
